Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1475
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1475
- **Title**: gh-1471 [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1471` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +673
- **Deletions**: -29
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T06:51:24Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T07:01:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.
- Shard step maps **both** bench secrets and the run block picks the resolved key by name (`${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}`) — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing, block stays env-driven and testable by the existing shell-harness family.
- `contextWindow: 200000` / `maxTokens: 16384` are declared explicitly for kimi (matches the catalog spec today, but immune to catalog drift); undeclared zai boots stay byte-identical.
- Artifact names (`tb-runs-shard-N`) intentionally unchanged — the merge job downloads by that pattern; run identity rides `run-name`/job name/summary header.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 328 tests, incl. new ProviderResolveStepTest + shape tests
dart test test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/model_roles/provider_catalog_test.dart
actionlint .github/workflows/bench.yml                  # clean
```

Owner setup (E2E blocker, not the code): add the repo secret `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, then smoke `tasks=hello-world, provider=kimi-for-coding, 1 shard`.

Note: `dart test test/cli/` (full dir) passes all 245 tests but the VM aborts in glibc at process shutdown on this runner — reproduced identically on clean `origin/main` (pre-existing environment issue, unrelated to this change).

<details>
<summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  DISP[workflow_dispatch provider choice] --> RES[setup: Resolve provider]
  SEC1[secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY] --> RES
  SEC2[secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY] --> RES
  RES -->|unknown choice / missing secret: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] fail, zero shard-hours| X1((fail))
  RES -->|outputs: type, config JSON, key env, run_label| SHARD[bench shard jobs]
  SHARD -->|FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG / key by name| AG[fa_agent.py → container env preconfig]
  AG --> MODEL[buildCliDefaultModel: declared contextWindow/maxTokens win]
  SHARD --> SUM[summary.py: Provider: run_label + pinned MODEL]
```

# gh-1471: [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Description

# [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Product frame

One sentence: **the terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the GLM/z.ai provider — every dispatch picks the provider (today: zai `glm-5.3-flash` or kimi-for-coding `k3-256k`), so a quota outage or a model-quality question on one provider never blocks or taints the whole benchmark programme, and cross-provider runs become directly comparable.**

Motivation (this run's scar tissue): full bench run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks (12 of them died on the FIRST request) when the z.ai GLM account quota ran out mid-run — raw 50.0% vs adjusted 60.9% on fairly-run tasks. A second provider both de-risks the quota single-point-of-failure and answers "model or harness?" by A/B running the same dataset.

## Current state (the hardcode)

- `.github/workflows/bench.yml:89` — `env.BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash` (single source of truth pin, PR #1351); shard env at `:213-215`: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: {"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"$BENCH_MODEL","apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI"}`, key from `secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY`.
- `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py` (`_env`, :104-115) — passes `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` + `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` (base64) + the api key (base64) into the task container; provider plumbing is ALREADY parameterized — only the workflow hardcodes the values.
- Summary/pricing: `MODEL: $BENCH_MODEL` pins the cost column (#1339 AC3); `bench/pricing.json` has no kimi entry today (cost would render `n/a`).
- Kimi-for-coding wiring (proven in the owner's own config + the ai-teammate factory's `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY` path): provider type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384.

## Design

### D1 — dispatch input `provider` (choice) + `custom` escape hatch

New `workflow_dispatch` input: `provider`, `type: choice`, options `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default) / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`. A resolve step maps the choice to the full triple and FAILS HARD on an unmapped value (never a silent fallthrough to the default).

**`custom`** exists so a new provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits: a second free-text input `provider-config` carries the whole provider config as JSON — `{"type": "...", "baseUrl": "...", "model": "...", "contextWindow": ..., "maxTokens": ...}` — passed through as `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` verbatim after validation:
- required: `baseUrl` (https:// only — plain http hard-fails), `model`; `type` optional (default `openai`-compatible);
- **the key NEVER rides the input** (dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata — a pasted key would leak): any field named like `apiKey`/`key`/`token`/`secret` hard-fails with a clear message;
- the key comes from a dedicated custom slot secret **`FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`** (rotate it per experiment), injected as a fixed `apiKeyEnvVar: FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM`; missing secret + custom selected = preflight fail (D3);
- validation is `jq`-level: parse errors and schema misses fail the resolve step before any shard starts.

### D2 — dedicated bench key for kimi

New repo secret **`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`** (owner adds it in repo settings — setup blocker, see Dependencies). Mapped to the container as the config's `apiKeyEnvVar` (e.g. `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH`). Deliberately NOT reusing `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`: the review factory and a multi-million-token bench must not contend for one quota (the exact failure mode this card exists to escape).

### D3 — missing-key preflight

The resolve step (or an early guard in the shard job) checks the selected provider's secret is non-empty and **fails the run in the first minute with a clear message** ("provider kimi-for-coding selected but secret FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY is not set") instead of burning 8 shards × hours on 429s. The check compares presence only — the key value is never echoed, logged, or written to artifacts (base64 passthrough stays).

### D4 — model capability fields reach the container

kimi needs `contextWindow: 200000` + `maxTokens: 16384` or the catalog/default mismatch silently truncates. Extend the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` JSON contract (and whatever consumes it — the CLI env-provider registry / fa-setup template) to carry optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`, OR pin them via the existing config path in `fa-setup.sh.j2`. Whichever lands, a zai run with NO new fields must remain byte-identical to today (REG-1).

### D5 — run identity carries provider+model

Run display name, summary header, and artifact metadata name the provider+model (e.g. `fa on terminal-bench · kimi-for-coding (k3-256k)`), so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/`/cost` views. (`name:` cannot read env contexts — resolve via the step output, same pattern as the existing comment at bench.yml:158.)

### D6 — pricing

Add a `k3-256k` entry to `bench/pricing.json`. Coding-plan pricing is subscription-based: record the per-MTok figure if published, else an explicit zero/n/a entry WITH a comment saying so — the summary must never invent a number (#1339 rule), `n/a` rendered knowingly is fine.

## Threat model / failure modes

- **Secret leak**: key only travels as env → base64 → container env; preflight prints presence, never value; session JSONL redaction (`[REDACTED:...]`) already covers the key material — verify in the kimi smoke run that the new env var name is redacted if it ever lands in a session.
- **Quota contention**: solved by D2 (dedicated key).
- **Silent default drift**: unmapped provider value = hard fail (D1); default stays zai-glm — existing scheduled/manual runs unchanged.
- **Comparability pollution**: D5 — a kimi run is unmistakable in the ledger.

## Test matrix

- **UT — resolve mapping** (`bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` family): each choice → expected (type, baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar); unknown input → fail; missing secret env → preflight failure message names the secret.
- **UT — custom validation**: valid JSON passthrough; rejects: non-JSON, missing baseUrl/model, `http://`, fields named `apiKey`/`key`/`token`/`secret` (case-insensitive); `type` defaulting.
- **UT — config contract**: `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` with/without `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` parses; zai-shaped legacy JSON (3 fields) unchanged.
- **REG-1 (blocking)**: dispatch with NO provider input (or the default) produces a shard env identical to today's (diff the resolved env in a dry run).
- **actionlint** on the edited workflow.
- **E2E smoke (post-secret)**: manual dispatch `tasks=hello-world`, `provider=kimi-for-coding`, 1 shard → task completes, summary shows kimi model + cost column behaves, session contains no raw key.
- **E2E A/B (post-secret, optional)**: same task subset on both providers for the comparability read.

## Acceptance

1. `provider` choice input live; default = today's behavior bit-for-bit.
2. kimi-for-coding selectable; resolves to type `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k` / dedicated key env.
2a. `custom` selectable: `provider-config` JSON flows verbatim into `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`; key ONLY via `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`; raw-key-looking fields / non-https baseUrl / unparseable JSON all hard-fail preflight.
3. Missing `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (kimi) or `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` (custom) = fast clear failure, zero shard-hours burned.
4. contextWindow/maxTokens plumbed for kimi; zai runs untouched.
5. Run identity + summary name provider/model; pricing.json entry added (number or explicit n/a).
6. Green: new UTs + REG-1 + actionlint + the hello-world kimi smoke (once the secret exists).

## Dependencies / setup

- **Owner action (blocker for E2E, not for the code)**: add repo secrets `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (kimi-for-coding) and — when the first custom experiment arrives — `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`.
- No changes to the dmtools factory / `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY` path.

## Non-goals

- A provider MATRIX (same dataset on N providers in one dispatch) — separate card if wanted; this one is a single-sel…

    "description": "# [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Product frame

One sentence: **the terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the GLM/z.ai provider — every dispatch picks the provider (today: zai `glm-5.3-flash` or kimi-for-coding `k3-256k`), so a quota outage or a model-quality question on one provider never blocks or taints the whole benchmark programme, and cross-provider runs become directly comparable.**

Motivation (this run's scar tissue): full bench run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks (12 of them died on the FIRST request) when the z.ai GLM account quota ran out mid-run — raw 50.0% vs adjusted 60.9% on fairly-run tasks. A second provider both de-risks the quota single-point-of-failure and answers "model or harness?" by A/B running the same dataset.

## Current state (the hardcode)

- `.github/workflows/bench.yml:89` — `env.BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash` (single source of truth pin, PR #1351); shard env at `:213-215`: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: {"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"$BENCH_MODEL","apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI"}`, key from `secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY`.
- `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py` (`_env`, :104-115) — passes `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` + `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` (base64) + the api key (base64) into the task container; provider plumbing is ALREADY parameterized — only the workflow hardcodes the values.
- Summary/pricing: `MODEL: $BENCH_MODEL` pins the cost column (#1339 AC3); `bench/pricing.json` has no kimi entry today (cost would render `n/a`).
- Kimi-for-coding wiring (proven in the owner's own config + the ai-teammate factory's `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY` path): provider type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384.

## Design

### D1 — dispatch input `provider` (choice) + `custom` escape hatch

New `workflow_dispatch` input: `provider`, `type: choice`, options `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default) / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`. A resolve step maps the choice to the full triple and FAILS HARD on an unmapped value (never a silent fallthrough to the default).

**`custom`** exists so a new provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits: a second free-text input `provider-config` carries the whole provider config as JSON — `{"type": "...", "baseUrl": "...", "model": "...", "contextWindow": ..., "maxTokens": ...}` — passed through as `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` verbatim after validation:
- required: `baseUrl` (https:// only — plain http hard-fails), `model`; `type` optional (default `openai`-compatible);
- **the key NEVER rides the input** (dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata — a pasted key would leak): any field named like `apiKey`/`key`/`token`/`secret` hard-fails with a clear message;
- the key comes from a dedicated custom slot secret **`FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`** (rotate it per experiment), injected as a fixed `apiKeyEnvVar: FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM`; missing secret + custom selected = preflight fail (D3);
- validation is `jq`-level: parse errors and schema misses fail the resolve step before any shard starts.

### D2 — dedicated bench key for kimi

New repo secret **`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`** (owner adds it in repo settings — setup blocker, see Dependencies). Mapped to the container as the config's `apiKeyEnvVar` (e.g. `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH`). Deliberately NOT reusing `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`: the review factory and a multi-million-token bench must not contend for one quota (the exact failure mode this card exists to escape).

### D3 — missing-key preflight

The resolve step (or an early guard in the shard job) checks the selected provider's secret is non-empty and **fails the run in the first minute with a clear message** ("provider kimi-for-coding selected but secret FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY is not set") instead of burning 8 shards × hours on 429s. The check compares presence only — the key value is never echoed, logged, or written to artifacts (base64 passthrough stays).

### D4 — model capability fields reach the container

kimi needs `contextWindow: 200000` + `maxTokens: 16384` or the catalog/default mismatch silently truncates. Extend the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` JSON contract (and whatever consumes it — the CLI env-provider registry / fa-setup template) to carry optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`, OR pin them via the existing config path in `fa-setup.sh.j2`. Whichever lands, a zai run with NO new fields must remain byte-identical to today (REG-1).

### D5 — run identity carries provider+model

Run display name, summary header, and artifact metadata name the provider+model (e.g. `fa on terminal-bench · kimi-for-coding (k3-256k)`), so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/`/cost` views. (`name:` cannot read env contexts — resolve via the step output, same pattern as the existing comment at bench.yml:158.)

### D6 — pricing

Add a `k3-256k` entry to `bench/pricing.json`. Coding-plan pricing is subscription-based: record the per-MTok figure if published, else an explicit zero/n/a entry WITH a comment saying so — the summary must never invent a number (#1339 rule), `n/a` rendered knowingly is fine.

- **Secret leak**: key only travels as env → base64 → container env; preflight prints presence, never value; session JSONL redaction (`[REDACTED:...]`) already covers the key material — verify in the kimi smoke run that the new env var name is redacted if it ever lands in a session.
- **Quota contention**: solved by D2 (dedicated key).
- **Silent default drift**: unmapped provider value = hard fail (D1); default stays zai-glm — existing scheduled/manual runs unchanged.
- **Comparability pollution**: D5 — a kimi run is unmistakable in the ledger.

- **UT — resolve mapping** (`bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` family): each choice → expected (type, baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar); unknown input → fail; missing secret env → preflight failure message names the secret.

name: Bench

# Runs the fa coding agent against terminal-bench on Linux runners
# (issue #125). The `dart build cli` bundle must be a Linux x64 binary to
# match the task container's arch — a macOS host bundle fails with
# "cannot execute binary file", so this cannot run locally on macOS.
#
# Sharded matrix (issue #132): the full terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 dataset
# is 80 tasks at ~11 min each — ~14 h sequential, past even the 6 h job
# cap. Shape: setup (build bundle, resolve task ids into shards) → one
# matrix job per shard → merge job aggregating overall accuracy. Small
# `tasks` inputs degenerate to a single-shard matrix, so the hello-world
# smoke path is unchanged.
#
# Issue #142 (baseline run 34576017658, 26/80 = 32.5%): shards are balanced
# by declared task budget (LPT) instead of contiguous split, tb runs with
# --global-timeout-multiplier 2 (the dataset's declared timeouts — median
# 360s agent / 60s test — assume fast models and warm container networks;
# the baseline lost trials to agents killed mid-progress and to test
# phases still apt-installing their own deps when the cap hit), and the
# bench job patches the downloaded dataset so debian:-based task images
# build again after Debian archived bullseye (expired Release file kills
# `apt-get update` during docker compose build).
#
# Issue #1122: the flat agent cap becomes a per-run ladder — `agent-timeout`
# (base cap seconds) plus optional `progress-extension` (deadline recedes
# while the agent's rendered output grows; idle window 120s, hard ceiling
# 4x base, decisions audited per trial). With both inputs absent the run
# is byte-for-byte today's behavior (dataset declared caps x multiplier;
# REG-1). E3 shard math: with extension on, worst case per task is the
# ceiling (4x agent-timeout) + test budget — the defaults fit the current
# LPT sizing below; raise the ceiling and shrink shards accordingly.
#
# Issue gh-1206 (run 37144207185): the DECLARED test budgets (tb default
# 60s = 120s effective at multiplier 2) classify slow-but-healthy verifier
# phases as test_timeout — jupyter-notebook-server died with the agent's
# pane DONE, the tests having burned their own budget on first-boot
# server startup + in-container dep installs. The test-side analog of the
# #1122 knobs: `test-timeout-floor` (default 120s declared = 240s
# effective) pads every task's max_test_timeout_sec up to the floor in
# the downloaded dataset (patch_test_timeouts.py — the same in-place
# patch mechanism as the Debian apt fix), and shard_tasks.py sizes shards
# on the padded budgets so LPT never under-counts. The cap is a cap, not
# a wait: fast verifier phases are unaffected (a full-dataset worst case
# grows < 10 min/shard); `0` restores the declared budgets.
#
# Issue gh-1407 (runs 37609468473 + 37736364517): the floor alone left
# repeat-offender tasks (jupyter-notebook-server, build-initramfs-qemu)
# test_timeout at the cap in every round — the budget measured runner
# luck, not agent capability. patch_test_timeouts.py additionally applies
# the per-task override table (test_budget_overrides.json, checked in
# next to it: runner-measured test-phase p95 per task, effective budget
# = max(declared, p95 x 1.5) — a slow-suite fix, NOT a global floor
# bump), and shard_tasks.py emits a ::warning:: fairness annotation when
# a planned task's effective test budget is still below its measured
# p95 (fairness_warnings job output), so a structurally-unpassable
# configuration is caught at planning time.
#
# Issue #1392 (bench round 3): retire the artificial timeout class. The
# ×4 ladder ceiling itself was the round-2 killer (play-zork died at 72
# productive minutes), so with progress-extension ON the ladder ceiling
# becomes an absolute one (3600s default, FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC)
# and the outer harness cap pins above THAT — a trial only dies by the
# adapter's verdict (stall / abs ceiling), never tb's flat wait_for. The
# experiment: split 8 shards, run at most `max-concurrent` (default 2) —
# GHA's strategy.max-parallel IS the semaphore. Shards are LPT-packed to
# the job cap minus 15 min headroom; the merge report degrades cancelled
# shards to a `coverage: X/N` note (never red from aggregation), carries
# per-request latency p50/p95 per concurrency level from each trial's
# bench_metrics.json, and names any agent_timeout trial whose session
# gaps never reached the 240s stall threshold (the round-2 contradiction,
# AC8).
# gh-1471 (run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks when the z.ai quota died
# mid-run): the provider stops being a hardcode — every dispatch picks
# zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to today) or kimi-for-coding
# k3-256k via a dedicated FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY (never the review factory's
# KIMI_REVIEW_KEY — one quota must not serve both). A setup-job resolve
# step maps the choice to the full provider triple and preflights the
# selected secret BEFORE any shard starts (presence only, never a value);
# the shard job names the provider+model (job `name:` CAN read needs
# outputs — unlike env), and the summary report tags it (BENCH_RUN_LABEL)
# so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/cost views.
run-name: fa bench · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is bui…

4. bin/fah_model.dart — new params but who passes them? Maybe fah_model should read the env preconfig too. Let me read the file.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1475
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1475
- **Title**: gh-1471 [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1471` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +673
- **Deletions**: -29
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T06:51:24Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T07:01:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.
- Shard step maps **both** bench secrets and the run block picks the resolved key by name (`${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}`) — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing, block stays env-driven and testable by the existing shell-harness family.
- `contextWindow: 200000` / `maxTokens: 16384` are declared explicitly for kimi (matches the catalog spec today, but immune to catalog drift); undeclared zai boots stay byte-identical.
- Artifact names (`tb-runs-shard-N`) intentionally unchanged — the merge job downloads by that pattern; run identity rides `run-name`/job name/summary header.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 328 tests, incl. new ProviderResolveStepTest + shape tests
dart test test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/model_roles/provider_catalog_test.dart
actionlint .github/workflows/bench.yml                  # clean
```

Owner setup (E2E blocker, not the code): add the repo secret `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, then smoke `tasks=hello-world, provider=kimi-for-coding, 1 shard`.

Note: `dart test test/cli/` (full dir) passes all 245 tests but the VM aborts in glibc at process shutdown on this runner — reproduced identically on clean `origin/main` (pre-existing environment issue, unrelated to this change).

# gh-1471: [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Description

# [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Product frame

One sentence: **the terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the GLM/z.ai provider — every dispatch picks the provider (today: zai `glm-5.3-flash` or kimi-for-coding `k3-256k`), so a quota outage or a model-quality question on one provider never blocks or taints the whole benchmark programme, and cross-provider runs become directly comparable.**

Motivation (this run's scar tissue): full bench run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks (12 of them died on the FIRST request) when the z.ai GLM account quota ran out mid-run — raw 50.0% vs adjusted 60.9% on fairly-run tasks. A second provider both de-risks the quota single-point-of-failure and answers "model or harness?" by A/B running the same dataset.

## Current state (the hardcode)

- `.github/workflows/bench.yml:89` — `env.BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash` (single source of truth pin, PR #1351); shard env at `:213-215`: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: {"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"$BENCH_MODEL","apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI"}`, key from `secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY`.
- `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py` (`_env`, :104-115) — passes `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` + `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` (base64) + the api key (base64) into the task container; provider plumbing is ALREADY parameterized — only the workflow hardcodes the values.
- Summary/pricing: `MODEL: $BENCH_MODEL` pins the cost column (#1339 AC3); `bench/pricing.json` has no kimi entry today (cost would render `n/a`).
- Kimi-for-coding wiring (proven in the owner's own config + the ai-teammate factory's `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY` path): provider type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384.

## Design

### D1 — dispatch input `provider` (choice) + `custom` escape hatch

New `workflow_dispatch` input: `provider`, `type: choice`, options `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default) / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`. A resolve step maps the choice to the full triple and FAILS HARD on an unmapped value (never a silent fallthrough to the default).

**`custom`** exists so a new provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits: a second free-text input `provider-config` carries the whole provider config as JSON — `{"type": "...", "baseUrl": "...", "model": "...", "contextWindow": ..., "maxTokens": ...}` — passed through as `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` verbatim after validation:
- required: `baseUrl` (https:// only — plain http hard-fails), `model`; `type` optional (default `openai`-compatible);
- **the key NEVER rides the input** (dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata — a pasted key would leak): any field named like `apiKey`/`key`/`token`/`secret` hard-fails with a clear message;
- the key comes from a dedicated custom slot secret **`FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`** (rotate it per experiment), injected as a fixed `apiKeyEnvVar: FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM`; missing secret + custom selected = preflight fail (D3);
- validation is `jq`-level: parse errors and schema misses fail the resolve step before any shard starts.

### D2 — dedicated bench key for kimi

New repo secret **`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`** (owner adds it in repo settings — setup blocker, see Dependencies). Mapped to the container as the config's `apiKeyEnvVar` (e.g. `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH`). Deliberately NOT reusing `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`: the review factory and a multi-million-token bench must not contend for one quota (the exact failure mode this card exists to escape).

### D3 — missing-key preflight

The resolve step (or an early guard in the shard job) checks the selected provider's secret is non-empty and **fails the run in the first minute with a clear message** ("provider kimi-for-coding selected but secret FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY is not set") instead of burning 8 shards × hours on 429s. The check compares presence only — the key value is never echoed, logged, or written to artifacts (base64 passthrough stays).

### D4 — model capability fields reach the container

kimi needs `contextWindow: 200000` + `maxTokens: 16384` or the catalog/default mismatch silently truncates. Extend the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` JSON contract (and whatever consumes it — the CLI env-provider registry / fa-setup template) to carry optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`, OR pin them via the existing config path in `fa-setup.sh.j2`. Whichever lands, a zai run with NO new fields must remain byte-identical to today (REG-1).

### D5 — run identity carries provider+model

Run display name, summary header, and artifact metadata name the provider+model (e.g. `fa on terminal-bench · kimi-for-coding (k3-256k)`), so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/`/cost` views. (`name:` cannot read env contexts — resolve via the step output, same pattern as the existing comment at bench.yml:158.)

### D6 — pricing

Add a `k3-256k` entry to `bench/pricing.json`. Coding-plan pricing is subscription-based: record the per-MTok figure if published, else an explicit zero/n/a entry WITH a comment saying so — the summary must never invent a number (#1339 rule), `n/a` rendered knowingly is fine.

## Threat model / failure modes

- **Secret leak**: key only travels as env → base64 → container env; preflight prints presence, never value; session JSONL redaction (`[REDACTED:...]`) already covers the key material — verify in the kimi smoke run that the new env var name is redacted if it ever lands in a session.
- **Quota contention**: solved by D2 (dedicated key).
- **Silent default drift**: unmapped provider value = hard fail (D1); default stays zai-glm — existing scheduled/manual runs unchanged.
- **Comparability pollution**: D5 — a kimi run is unmistakable in the ledger.

## Test matrix

- **UT — resolve mapping** (`bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` family): each choice → expected (type, baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar); unknown input → fail; missing secret env → preflight failure message names the secret.
- **UT — custom validation**: valid JSON passthrough; rejects: non-JSON, missing baseUrl/model, `http://`, fields named `apiKey`/`key`/`token`/`secret` (case-insensitive); `type` defaulting.
- **UT — config contract**: `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` with/without `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` parses; zai-shaped legacy JSON (3 fields) unchanged.
- **REG-1 (blocking)**: dispatch with NO provider input (or the default) produces a shard env identical to today's (diff the resolved env in a dry run).
- **actionlint** on the edited workflow.
- **E2E smoke (post-secret)**: manual dispatch `tasks=hello-world`, `provider=kimi-for-coding`, 1 shard → task completes, summary shows kimi model + cost column behaves, session contains no raw key.
- **E2E A/B (post-secret, optional)**: same task subset on both providers for the comparability read.

## Acceptance

1. `provider` choice input live; default = today's behavior bit-for-bit.
2. kimi-for-coding selectable; resolves to type `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k` / dedicated key env.
2a. `custom` selectable: `provider-config` JSON flows verbatim into `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`; key ONLY via `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`; raw-key-looking fields / non-https baseUrl / unparseable JSON all hard-fail preflight.
3. Missing `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (kimi) or `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` (custom) = fast clear failure, zero shard-hours burned.
4. contextWindow/maxTokens plumbed for kimi; zai runs untouched.
5. Run identity + summary name provider/model; pricing.json entry added (number or explicit n/a).
6. Green: new UTs + REG-1 + actionlint + the hello-world kimi smoke (once the secret exists).

## Dependencies / setup

- **Owner action (blocker for E2E, not for the code)**: add repo secrets `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (kimi-for-coding) and — when the first custom experiment arrives — `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`.
- No changes to the dmtools factory / `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY` path.

## Non-goals

- A provider MATRIX (same dataset on N providers in one dispatch) — separate card if wanted; this one is a single-sel…

    "description": "# [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Product frame

One sentence: **the terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the GLM/z.ai provider — every dispatch picks the provider (today: zai `glm-5.3-flash` or kimi-for-coding `k3-256k`), so a quota outage or a model-quality question on one provider never blocks or taints the whole benchmark programme, and cross-provider runs become directly comparable.**

Motivation (this run's scar tissue): full bench run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks (12 of them died on the FIRST request) when the z.ai GLM account quota ran out mid-run — raw 50.0% vs adjusted 60.9% on fairly-run tasks. A second provider both de-risks the quota single-point-of-failure and answers "model or harness?" by A/B running the same dataset.

## Current state (the hardcode)

- `.github/workflows/bench.yml:89` — `env.BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash` (single source of truth pin, PR #1351); shard env at `:213-215`: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: {"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"$BENCH_MODEL","apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI"}`, key from `secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY`.
- `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py` (`_env`, :104-115) — passes `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` + `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` (base64) + the api key (base64) into the task container; provider plumbing is ALREADY parameterized — only the workflow hardcodes the values.
- Summary/pricing: `MODEL: $BENCH_MODEL` pins the cost column (#1339 AC3); `bench/pricing.json` has no kimi entry today (cost would render `n/a`).
- Kimi-for-coding wiring (proven in the owner's own config + the ai-teammate factory's `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY` path): provider type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384.

## Design

### D1 — dispatch input `provider` (choice) + `custom` escape hatch

New `workflow_dispatch` input: `provider`, `type: choice`, options `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default) / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`. A resolve step maps the choice to the full triple and FAILS HARD on an unmapped value (never a silent fallthrough to the default).

**`custom`** exists so a new provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits: a second free-text input `provider-config` carries the whole provider config as JSON — `{"type": "...", "baseUrl": "...", "model": "...", "contextWindow": ..., "maxTokens": ...}` — passed through as `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` verbatim after validation:
- required: `baseUrl` (https:// only — plain http hard-fails), `model`; `type` optional (default `openai`-compatible);
- **the key NEVER rides the input** (dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata — a pasted key would leak): any field named like `apiKey`/`key`/`token`/`secret` hard-fails with a clear message;
- the key comes from a dedicated custom slot secret **`FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`** (rotate it per experiment), injected as a fixed `apiKeyEnvVar: FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM`; missing secret + custom selected = preflight fail (D3);
- validation is `jq`-level: parse errors and schema misses fail the resolve step before any shard starts.

### D2 — dedicated bench key for kimi

New repo secret **`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`** (owner adds it in repo settings — setup blocker, see Dependencies). Mapped to the container as the config's `apiKeyEnvVar` (e.g. `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH`). Deliberately NOT reusing `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`: the review factory and a multi-million-token bench must not contend for one quota (the exact failure mode this card exists to escape).

### D3 — missing-key preflight

The resolve step (or an early guard in the shard job) checks the selected provider's secret is non-empty and **fails the run in the first minute with a clear message** ("provider kimi-for-coding selected but secret FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY is not set") instead of burning 8 shards × hours on 429s. The check compares presence only — the key value is never echoed, logged, or written to artifacts (base64 passthrough stays).

### D4 — model capability fields reach the container

kimi needs `contextWindow: 200000` + `maxTokens: 16384` or the catalog/default mismatch silently truncates. Extend the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` JSON contract (and whatever consumes it — the CLI env-provider registry / fa-setup template) to carry optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`, OR pin them via the existing config path in `fa-setup.sh.j2`. Whichever lands, a zai run with NO new fields must remain byte-identical to today (REG-1).

### D5 — run identity carries provider+model

Run display name, summary header, and artifact metadata name the provider+model (e.g. `fa on terminal-bench · kimi-for-coding (k3-256k)`), so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/`/cost` views. (`name:` cannot read env contexts — resolve via the step output, same pattern as the existing comment at bench.yml:158.)

### D6 — pricing

Add a `k3-256k` entry to `bench/pricing.json`. Coding-plan pricing is subscription-based: record the per-MTok figure if published, else an explicit zero/n/a entry WITH a comment saying so — the summary must never invent a number (#1339 rule), `n/a` rendered knowingly is fine.

- **Secret leak**: key only travels as env → base64 → container env; preflight prints presence, never value; session JSONL redaction (`[REDACTED:...]`) already covers the key material — verify in the kimi smoke run that the new env var name is redacted if it ever lands in a session.
- **Quota contention**: solved by D2 (dedicated key).
- **Silent default drift**: unmapped provider value = hard fail (D1); default stays zai-glm — existing scheduled/manual runs unchanged.
- **Comparability pollution**: D5 — a kimi run is unmistakable in the ledger.

## Test matrix

- **UT — resolve mapping** (`bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` family): each choice → expected (type, baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar); unknown input → fail; missing secret env → preflight failure message names the secret.

- **UT — config contract**: `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` with/without `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` parses; zai-shaped legacy JSON (3 fields) unchanged.
- **REG-1 (blocking)**: dispatch with NO provider input (or the default) produces a shard env identical to today's (diff the resolved env in a dry run).

- **E2E smoke (post-secret)**: manual dispatch `tasks=hello-world`, `provider=kimi-for-coding`, 1 shard → task completes, summary shows kimi model + cost column behaves, session contains no raw key.
- **E2E A/B (post-secret, optional)**: same task subset on both providers for the comparability read.

3. Missing `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (kimi) or `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` (custom) = fast clear failure, zero shard-hours burned.
4. contextWindow/maxTokens plumbed for kimi; zai runs untouched.
5. Run identity + summary name provider/model; pricing.json entry added (number or explicit n/a).
6. Green: new UTs + REG-1 + actionlint + the hello-world kimi smoke (once the secret exists).

+    Same text-slicing contract as [_shard_run_block]: the block is

+    arrive via the step env), so no GitHub expression may appear inside.

+    lines = _BENCH_YML.read_text().splitlines()
+    for i, line in enumerate(lines):

+            continue
+        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())

+        for candidate in lines[i + 1 :]:
+            if candidate.strip() and (len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())) <= indent:

blocks.text:
name: Bench

# Runs the fa coding agent against terminal-bench on Linux runners
# (issue #125). The `dart build cli` bundle must be a Linux x64 binary to
# match the task container's arch — a macOS host bundle fails with
# "cannot execute binary file", so this cannot run locally on macOS.
#
# Sharded matrix (issue #132): the full terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 dataset
# is 80 tasks at ~11 min each — ~14 h sequential, past even the 6 h job
# cap. Shape: setup (build bundle, resolve task ids into shards) → one
# matrix job per shard → merge job aggregating overall accuracy. Small
# `tasks` inputs degenerate to a single-shard matrix, so the hello-world
# smoke path is unchanged.
#
# Issue #142 (baseline run 34576017658, 26/80 = 32.5%): shards are balanced
# by declared task budget (LPT) instead of contiguous split, tb runs with
# --global-timeout-multiplier 2 (the dataset's declared timeouts — median
# 360s agent / 60s test — assume fast models and warm container networks;
# the baseline lost trials to agents killed mid-progress and to test
# phases still apt-installing their own deps when the cap hit), and the
# bench job patches the downloaded dataset so debian:-based task images
# build again after Debian archived bullseye (expired Release file kills
# `apt-get update` during docker compose build).
#
# Issue #1122: the flat agent cap becomes a per-run ladder — `agent-timeout`
# (base cap seconds) plus optional `progress-extension` (deadline recedes
# while the agent's rendered output grows; idle window 120s, hard ceiling
# 4x base, decisions audited per trial). With both inputs absent the run
# is byte-for-byte today's behavior (dataset declared caps x multiplier;
# REG-1). E3 shard math: with extension on, worst case per task is the
# ceiling (4x agent-timeout) + test budget — the defaults fit the current
# LPT sizing below; raise the ceiling and shrink shards accordingly.
#
# Issue gh-1206 (run 37144207185): the DECLARED test budgets (tb default
# 60s = 120s effective at multiplier 2) classify slow-but-healthy verifier
# phases as test_timeout — jupyter-notebook-server died with the agent's
# pane DONE, the tests having burned their own budget on first-boot
# server startup + in-container dep installs. The test-side analog of the
# #1122 knobs: `test-timeout-floor` (default 120s declared = 240s
# effective) pads every task's max_test_timeout_sec up to the floor in
# the downloaded dataset (patch_test_timeouts.py — the same in-place
# patch mechanism as the Debian apt fix), and shard_tasks.py sizes shards
# on the padded budgets so LPT never under-counts. The cap is a cap, not
# a wait: fast verifier phases are unaffected (a full-dataset worst case
# grows < 10 min/shard); `0` restores the declared budgets.
#
# Issue gh-1407 (runs 37609468473 + 37736364517): the floor alone left
# repeat-offender tasks (jupyter-notebook-server, build-initramfs-qemu)
# test_timeout at the cap in every round — the budget measured runner
# luck, not agent capability. patch_test_timeouts.py additionally applies
# the per-task override table (test_budget_overrides.json, checked in
# next to it: runner-measured test-phase p95 per task, effective budget
# = max(declared, p95 x 1.5) — a slow-suite fix, NOT a global floor
# bump), and shard_tasks.py emits a ::warning:: fairness annotation when
# a planned task's effective test budget is still below its measured
# p95 (fairness_warnings job output), so a structurally-unpassable
# configuration is caught at planning time.
#
# Issue #1392 (bench round 3): retire the artificial timeout class. The
# ×4 ladder ceiling itself was the round-2 killer (play-zork died at 72
# productive minutes), so with progress-extension ON the ladder ceiling
# becomes an absolute one (3600s default, FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC)
# and the outer harness cap pins above THAT — a trial only dies by the
# adapter's verdict (stall / abs ceiling), never tb's flat wait_for. The
# experiment: split 8 shards, run at most `max-concurrent` (default 2) —
# GHA's strategy.max-parallel IS the semaphore. Shards are LPT-packed to
# the job cap minus 15 min headroom; the merge report degrades cancelled
# shards to a `coverage: X/N` note (never red from aggregation), carries
# per-request latency p50/p95 per concurrency level from each trial's
# bench_metrics.json, and names any agent_timeout trial whose session
# gaps never reached the 240s stall threshold (the round-2 contradiction,
# AC8).
# gh-1471 (run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks when the z.ai quota died
# mid-run): the provider stops being a hardcode — every dispatch picks
# zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to today) or kimi-for-coding
# k3-256k via a dedicated FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY (never the review factory's
# KIMI_REVIEW_KEY — one quota must not serve both). A setup-job resolve
# step maps the choice to the full provider triple and preflights the
# selected secret BEFORE any shard starts (presence only, never a value);
# the shard job names the provider+model (job `name:` CAN read needs
# outputs — unlike env), and the summary report tags it (BENCH_RUN_LABEL)
# so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/cost views.
run-name: fa bench · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:

    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is bui…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1475
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1475
- **Title**: gh-1471 [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1471` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +673
- **Deletions**: -29
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T06:51:24Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T07:01:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.

# gh-1471: [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Description

# [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Product frame

One sentence: **the terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the GLM/z.ai provider — every dispatch picks the provider (today: zai `glm-5.3-flash` or kimi-for-coding `k3-256k`), so a quota outage or a model-quality question on one provider never blocks or taints the whole benchmark programme, and cross-provider runs become directly comparable.**

Motivation (this run's scar tissue): full bench run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks (12 of them died on the FIRST request) when the z.ai GLM account quota ran out mid-run — raw 50.0% vs adjusted 60.9% on fairly-run tasks. A second provider both de-risks the quota single-point-of-failure and answers "model or harness?" by A/B running the same dataset.

## Current state (the hardcode)

- `.github/workflows/bench.yml:89` — `env.BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash` (single source of truth pin, PR #1351); shard env at `:213-215`: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: {"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"$BENCH_MODEL","apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI"}`, key from `secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY`.
- `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py` (`_env`, :104-115) — passes `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` + `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` (base64) + the api key (base64) into the task container; provider plumbing is ALREADY parameterized — only the workflow hardcodes the values.
- Summary/pricing: `MODEL: $BENCH_MODEL` pins the cost column (#1339 AC3); `bench/pricing.json` has no kimi entry today (cost would render `n/a`).
- Kimi-for-coding wiring (proven in the owner's own config + the ai-teammate factory's `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY` path): provider type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384.

## Design

### D1 — dispatch input `provider` (choice) + `custom` escape hatch

New `workflow_dispatch` input: `provider`, `type: choice`, options `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default) / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`. A resolve step maps the choice to the full triple and FAILS HARD on an unmapped value (never a silent fallthrough to the default).

**`custom`** exists so a new provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits: a second free-text input `provider-config` carries the whole provider config as JSON — `{"type": "...", "baseUrl": "...", "model": "...", "contextWindow": ..., "maxTokens": ...}` — passed through as `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` verbatim after validation:
- required: `baseUrl` (https:// only — plain http hard-fails), `model`; `type` optional (default `openai`-compatible);
- **the key NEVER rides the input** (dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata — a pasted key would leak): any field named like `apiKey`/`key`/`token`/`secret` hard-fails with a clear message;
- the key comes from a dedicated custom slot secret **`FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`** (rotate it per experiment), injected as a fixed `apiKeyEnvVar: FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM`; missing secret + custom selected = preflight fail (D3);
- validation is `jq`-level: parse errors and schema misses fail the resolve step before any shard starts.

### D2 — dedicated bench key for kimi

New repo secret **`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`** (owner adds it in repo settings — setup blocker, see Dependencies). Mapped to the container as the config's `apiKeyEnvVar` (e.g. `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH`). Deliberately NOT reusing `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`: the review factory and a multi-million-token bench must not contend for one quota (the exact failure mode this card exists to escape).

### D3 — missing-key preflight

The resolve step (or an early guard in the shard job) checks the selected provider's secret is non-empty and **fails the run in the first minute with a clear message** ("provider kimi-for-coding selected but secret FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY is not set") instead of burning 8 shards × hours on 429s. The check compares presence only — the key value is never echoed, logged, or written to artifacts (base64 passthrough stays).

### D4 — model capability fields reach the container

kimi needs `contextWindow: 200000` + `maxTokens: 16384` or the catalog/default mismatch silently truncates. Extend the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` JSON contract (and whatever consumes it — the CLI env-provider registry / fa-setup template) to carry optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`, OR pin them via the existing config path in `fa-setup.sh.j2`. Whichever lands, a zai run with NO new fields must remain byte-identical to today (REG-1).

### D5 — run identity carries provider+model

Run display name, summary header, and artifact metadata name the provider+model (e.g. `fa on terminal-bench · kimi-for-coding (k3-256k)`), so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/`/cost` views. (`name:` cannot read env contexts — resolve via the step output, same pattern as the existing comment at bench.yml:158.)

### D6 — pricing

Add a `k3-256k` entry to `bench/pricing.json`. Coding-plan pricing is subscription-based: record the per-MTok figure if published, else an explicit zero/n/a entry WITH a comment saying so — the summary must never invent a number (#1339 rule), `n/a` rendered knowingly is fine.

## Threat model / failure modes

- **Secret leak**: key only travels as env → base64 → container env; preflight prints presence, never value; session JSONL redaction (`[REDACTED:...]`) already covers the key material — verify in the kimi smoke run that the new env var name is redacted if it ever lands in a session.
- **Quota contention**: solved by D2 (dedicated key).
- **Silent default drift**: unmapped provider value = hard fail (D1); default stays zai-glm — existing scheduled/manual runs unchanged.
- **Comparability pollution**: D5 — a kimi run is unmistakable in the ledger.

## Test matrix

- **UT — resolve mapping** (`bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` family): each choice → expected (type, baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar); unknown input → fail; missing secret env → preflight failure message names the secret.
- **UT — custom validation**: valid JSON passthrough; rejects: non-JSON, missing baseUrl/model, `http://`, fields named `apiKey`/`key`/`token`/`secret` (case-insensitive); `type` defaulting.
- **UT — config contract**: `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` with/without `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` parses; zai-shaped legacy JSON (3 fields) unchanged.
- **REG-1 (blocking)**: dispatch with NO provider input (or the default) produces a shard env identical to today's (diff the resolved env in a dry run).
- **actionlint** on the edited workflow.
- **E2E smoke (post-secret)**: manual dispatch `tasks=hello-world`, `provider=kimi-for-coding`, 1 shard → task completes, summary shows kimi model + cost column behaves, session contains no raw key.
- **E2E A/B (post-secret, optional)**: same task subset on both providers for the comparability read.

## Acceptance

1. `provider` choice input live; default = today's behavior bit-for-bit.
2. kimi-for-coding selectable; resolves to type `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k` / dedicated key env.
2a. `custom` selectable: `provider-config` JSON flows verbatim into `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE`/`FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`; key ONLY via `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`; raw-key-looking fields / non-https baseUrl / unparseable JSON all hard-fail preflight.
3. Missing `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (kimi) or `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` (custom) = fast clear failure, zero shard-hours burned.
4. contextWindow/maxTokens plumbed for kimi; zai runs untouched.
5. Run identity + summary name provider/model; pricing.json entry added (number or explicit n/a).
6. Green: new UTs + REG-1 + actionlint + the hello-world kimi smoke (once the secret exists).

## Dependencies / setup

- **Owner action (blocker for E2E, not for the code)**: add repo secrets `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (kimi-for-coding) and — when the first custom experiment arrives — `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`.
- No changes to the dmtools factory / `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY` path.

## Non-goals

- A provider MATRIX (same dataset on N providers in one dispatch) — separate card if wanted; this one is a single-sel…

+    Same text-slicing contract as [_shard_run_block]: the block is
+    identified by its body (the provider_config printf), so unrelated
+    `run:` blocks never match. The block is env-driven (inputs/secrets

blocks.text:
name: Bench

# Runs the fa coding agent against terminal-bench on Linux runners
# (issue #125). The `dart build cli` bundle must be a Linux x64 binary to
# match the task container's arch — a macOS host bundle fails with
# "cannot execute binary file", so this cannot run locally on macOS.
#
# Sharded matrix (issue #132): the full terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 dataset
# is 80 tasks at ~11 min each — ~14 h sequential, past even the 6 h job
# cap. Shape: setup (build bundle, resolve task ids into shards) → one
# matrix job per shard → merge job aggregating overall accuracy. Small
# `tasks` inputs degenerate to a single-shard matrix, so the hello-world
# smoke path is unchanged.
#
# Issue #142 (baseline run 34576017658, 26/80 = 32.5%): shards are balanced
# by declared task budget (LPT) instead of contiguous split, tb runs with
# --global-timeout-multiplier 2 (the dataset's declared timeouts — median
# 360s agent / 60s test — assume fast models and warm container networks;
# the baseline lost trials to agents killed mid-progress and to test
# phases still apt-installing their own deps when the cap hit), and the
# bench job patches the downloaded dataset so debian:-based task images
# build again after Debian archived bullseye (expired Release file kills
# `apt-get update` during docker compose build).
#
# Issue #1122: the flat agent cap becomes a per-run ladder — `agent-timeout`
# (base cap seconds) plus optional `progress-extension` (deadline recedes
# while the agent's rendered output grows; idle window 120s, hard ceiling
# 4x base, decisions audited per trial). With both inputs absent the run
# is byte-for-byte today's behavior (dataset declared caps x multiplier;
# REG-1). E3 shard math: with extension on, worst case per task is the
# ceiling (4x agent-timeout) + test budget — the defaults fit the current
# LPT sizing below; raise the ceiling and shrink shards accordingly.
#
# Issue gh-1206 (run 37144207185): the DECLARED test budgets (tb default
# 60s = 120s effective at multiplier 2) classify slow-but-healthy verifier
# phases as test_timeout — jupyter-notebook-server died with the agent's
# pane DONE, the tests having burned their own budget on first-boot
# server startup + in-container dep installs. The test-side analog of the
# #1122 knobs: `test-timeout-floor` (default 120s declared = 240s
# effective) pads every task's max_test_timeout_sec up to the floor in
# the downloaded dataset (patch_test_timeouts.py — the same in-place
# patch mechanism as the Debian apt fix), and shard_tasks.py sizes shards
# on the padded budgets so LPT never under-counts. The cap is a cap, not
# a wait: fast verifier phases are unaffected (a full-dataset worst case
# grows < 10 min/shard); `0` restores the declared budgets.
#
# Issue gh-1407 (runs 37609468473 + 37736364517): the floor alone left
# repeat-offender tasks (jupyter-notebook-server, build-initramfs-qemu)
# test_timeout at the cap in every round — the budget measured runner
# luck, not agent capability. patch_test_timeouts.py additionally applies
# the per-task override table (test_budget_overrides.json, checked in
# next to it: runner-measured test-phase p95 per task, effective budget
# = max(declared, p95 x 1.5) — a slow-suite fix, NOT a global floor
# bump), and shard_tasks.py emits a ::warning:: fairness annotation when
# a planned task's effective test budget is still below its measured
# p95 (fairness_warnings job output), so a structurally-unpassable
# configuration is caught at planning time.
#
# Issue #1392 (bench round 3): retire the artificial timeout class. The
# ×4 ladder ceiling itself was the round-2 killer (play-zork died at 72
# productive minutes), so with progress-extension ON the ladder ceiling
# becomes an absolute one (3600s default, FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC)
# and the outer harness cap pins above THAT — a trial only dies by the
# adapter's verdict (stall / abs ceiling), never tb's flat wait_for. The
# experiment: split 8 shards, run at most `max-concurrent` (default 2) —
# GHA's strategy.max-parallel IS the semaphore. Shards are LPT-packed to
# the job cap minus 15 min headroom; the merge report degrades cancelled
# shards to a `coverage: X/N` note (never red from aggregation), carries
# per-request latency p50/p95 per concurrency level from each trial's
# bench_metrics.json, and names any agent_timeout trial whose session
# gaps never reached the 240s stall threshold (the round-2 contradiction,
# AC8).
# gh-1471 (run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks when the z.ai quota died
# mid-run): the provider stops being a hardcode — every dispatch picks
# zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to today) or kimi-for-coding
# k3-256k via a dedicated FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY (never the review factory's
# KIMI_REVIEW_KEY — one quota must not serve both). A setup-job resolve
# step maps the choice to the full provider triple and preflights the
# selected secret BEFORE any shard starts (presence only, never a value);
# the shard job names the provider+model (job `name:` CAN read needs
# outputs — unlike env), and the summary report tags it (BENCH_RUN_LABEL)
# so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/cost views.
run-name: fa bench · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is bui…

Now let me check:
1. fa_agent.py — how the key reaches the container (does it read apiKeyEnvVar from FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG? Does FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV need to be in _CONN_ENV_KEYS?).
2. capability_resolver floors.
3. fah_runapp.dart call site (already seen passes faPreconfig values).
4. bin/fah_model.dart — new params but who passes them? Maybe fah_model should read the env preconfig too. Let me read the file.
5. Check `run-name` — with `·` char fine.

Also check whether the kimi provider type `kimi` is a known catalog provider type (resolveCliProviderSpec('kimi')). The catalog test uses buildCliDefaultModel('kimi', modelId: 'k3-256k') so presumably yes.

Also check test_summary_1392 `_results` helper etc. — fine.

# Shared extraction lives one level up (bench/fa_usage.py); PYTHONPATH only

_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

# Never-started trials: the only outcomes where fa cannot have produced a
# session, so the issue #1123 usage fold is skipped (gh-1209 — every
# outcome where the agent actually ran gets the fold).

    {
        FailureMode.AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED,
        FailureMode.UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR,
